bufferLimits.comment: The maximum supported size of an ArrayBuffer is the maximum size that can be allocated in JavaScript. This maximum is defined by the maximum size PartitionAlloc can allocate. We limit the maximum size of ArrayBuffers we support to avoid integer overflows in the WebGL implementation. WebGL stores the data size as uint32_t, so if sizes just below uint32_t::max() were passed in, integer overflows could happen. The limit defined here is (2GB-2MB), which should be enough buffer to avoid integer overflow. This limit should restrict the usability of WebGL2 only insignificantly, as JavaScript cannot allocate bigger ArrayBuffers anyways. Only with WebAssembly it is possible to allocate bigger ArrayBuffers.
